concerns.message: Two existing scenarios use a single browser, but the lobby now needs 2 players to start. `sail-and-dock` (tests/e2e/sea.spec.ts:35) uses one page. `join-private-match` (tests/e2e/private-match.spec.ts:10) asserts `hud-players`=1, `hud-dock`='at sea', a ship drawn on the canvas and cleared fog, which all assume a started sea view. Acceptance 6 says to start these scenarios through the lobby, and acceptance 1 says 1 player can't start.
concerns.consequence: The worker must either join a second headless player (packages/test-tools can be imported from Node in the Playwright test) or add a start bypass. A bypass would quietly break 'start through the lobby'. Either way, rework in both specs that the plan doesn't foresee. The worker should use a headless second joiner and keep join-private-match's assertions to the lobby view.

concerns.message: Today no room test has spawn protection: `createEncounterState` is called without `spawnProtected`, and no test mentions spawnProtection. After this change, control-started gives every player 45 s of protection. `sea-duel` grapples right after joining (a protected defender is ineligible), and so do tests/integration/seaDuel*.test.ts and the rubbings tests. The e2e server is one process with env-based settings, and the Playwright per-test timeout is 60 s. The plan's list of test-only settings (pinned secret, short durations, pinned layout) has no spawn-protection override.
concerns.consequence: `sea-duel` and several integration tests fail or time out: 45 s of protection plus the ready countdown exceeds 60 s. The worker needs another env/tuning knob (encounters.spawnProtectionTicks) that is documented and off by default. The integration and web unit test that proves 45 s by default must run without it.

concerns.message: The ledger has no operation that ends a duel in the theft-choice window without theft. `reportDuelResult` only accepts duels in phase `fighting`. A duel whose fight ended but is still `choosing` when the claim or deadline ends the match gets `duel-ended-without-theft` from stepClaim. Yet `advanceLedger` will later commit the default theft. The room also keeps calling `quitPlayer`/`advanceLedger` as players leave the results screen.
concerns.consequence: After the end, the ledger, the HUD notices and the frozen results can disagree: a theft appears after the match ended, breaking 'outcomes freeze'. Or, if the worker stops driving the ledger, a leave removes a ship the ledger still counts and trips the room's own `checkInvariants`. Before writing the end path, decide that the room freezes ledger mutations except quit/leave bookkeeping after `match-ended`. Report the missing ledger operation as a gap rather than patching around it.

concerns.message: `abandoned` depends on a world tick running after the last leave. MatchRoom has no `autoDispose` override and no `onDispose`. When the last client leaves with consent, Colyseus disposes the room right after `onLeave`, before any `stepMatch` sees the leave reports. The PRD has no results store to show the outcome either.
concerns.consequence: The 'abandoned when everyone leaves' integration test can't observe an ending, or passes only by chance. The room should step the match itself in `onLeave` (or `onDispose`) when nobody is left, and expose the end to tests through a server-side hook or log.

concerns.message: The seed design allows `hashState({secret, system})` over a master secret drawn with the existing `RandomSource` (`randomInt(0, 2**32)`). hashState is an unkeyed 64-bit FNV, and a 32-bit master secret can be brute-forced: the client ships the same deal code, so a player who observes the ledger deal (and later the ruins and fruit deals) can narrow the 2^32 candidates and then compute the final socket. Separately, the intel module takes its own seed (`createIntelState(config, seed)`), and the plan's list of systems leaves it out.
concerns.consequence: The must-fix correlation is only renamed: every system still hangs off one brute-forceable 32-bit value. The intel seed will probably get the ledger seed or a constant 0, so one raw seed goes to two systems again. Use `randomBytes(32)` with `createHmac('sha256', secret).update(system)` and take 32 bits. Add 'intel' as a derived system now.

concerns.message: The reveals exist only as one-shot intel messages (`final-sector`, `final-route`, `final-route-inactive`). Colyseus messages aren't replayed on reconnect. A holder who drops and returns within the §12 reservation, or reloads the page, loses the compass and route marker; everyone else loses the sector banner and state.
concerns.consequence: This silently breaks §12's 'reattach to the current authoritative state' for the one player about to win, and no planned test catches it. Also keep the reveal in synced state: the sector publicly after the first full set, and route {x, y, active} in the holder's private status. The hidden-information test should then check state patches as well as messages.

concerns.message: Exact-tick acceptance cases (a claim completing on the deadline tick, a reservation on the tick a claim would complete) run on the real 20 Hz Colyseus clock with inputs arriving over websockets. MatchRoom has no manual or stepped clock.
concerns.consequence: If these tests are driven purely by timed client input, they will be flaky, and the verifier runs the suite once. The deterministic route: tests reach the room in-process (`roomOf`), read `matchState.worldTick`, and call `placeShip` in the same synchronous block. With E already held and the full set in hand, this puts the channel start on a known tick, e.g. D − channelTicks. Otherwise, add a documented test-only stepped clock.

concerns.message: The gating and hidden information around the lobby and the claim are implicit. (a) Before control-started, the helm, grapple and E must be neutral, or players can sail and collect in the lobby: stepMatch counts nothing before control start, so the results' `rubbingsHeld` would disagree with the ledger. (b) The claim prompt, circle status and progress must go only to a full-set holder, or 'you are in the treasure circle' leaks the socket (§16). (c) admission.ts:42 reports a locked room as full, so locking at start gives late joiners 'match full' instead of a clear 'already started' message. (d) Only the test fault hook leads to `aborted`: an exception in `advance()` would throw on every tick.
concerns.consequence: Results numbers are off for players who act early, hidden information leaks, late joiners get a misleading refusal, and a real server fault leaves a stuck room instead of an aborted match. Wrap `advance()` so an exception reports `fault`.

simpler_alternative: Deliver the reveals as synced state, not one-shot messages. The public match schema carries `finalSector` (set when intel emits `final-sector`). The holder's private StateView status carries `route: {x, y, active}` and the claim progress. The web client shows the banners when that state changes. This removes the reconnect gap and puts the hidden-information check on one channel: assert over state patches plus the minute-20/28 broadcast messages. It also leaves the persisted per-player view that `intel-online`'s journal will need anyway. Pair it with an HMAC-SHA256 derivation over a 256-bit secret from `randomBytes`, which is simpler and stronger than hashState over a 32-bit `randomInt`.
cheap_experiment: Before building the claim and endings suites (about 30 minutes), spike one integration test through the real room. Use tuning with readyTicks=20, spawnProtectionTicks=0, deadlineTicks=channelTicks+60 and a pinned layout. Have two headless clients start from the lobby. The host collects both types, holds E, and gets `placeShip` onto the claim tile when `worldTick === deadlineTick − channelTicks − 1`, read in-process. Run it 20 times and record whether `claim-completed` lands on the deadline tick and the match ends with reason `claim`. In the same spike, have both clients leave with consent and check whether `abandoned` is ever recorded before Colyseus disposes the room. The first result decides between in-process tick-aligned placement and a test-only stepped clock. The second decides whether the room must step the match inside `onLeave`/`onDispose`.
